answer: An agent economy can resist Sybils by requiring each identity to lock a bond that is slashed when its behaviour echoes another identity's. Like shale laid down in distinct layers, every agent builds a unique, time-stamped history of work signed with its own quill, its private key. When two identities submit near-identical outputs or timing patterns, auditors flag the echo and slash both bonds. One fake identity is cheap, but maintaining dozens of distinct, non-echoing histories while risking a bond on each is expensive, and duplication still forfeits the bond.
